title: About Root Certificates for Zero Trust Browser in Internet & SaaS

blocks.text: The isolation browser trusts all the well-known certificate authorities trusted by Chromium. In addition, Zscaler also provides administrators with the capability to upload root certificates of their choice that they want the isolated browser to trust for successful SSL communication. You can associate these uploaded certificates with the isolation profiles that are created for Internet & SaaS (ZIA). To learn more, see Creating Isolation Profiles for Internet & SaaS.
On the Root Certificates page (Internet Access > Resources > Root Certificates), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View a list of existing root certificates and their details. For each root certificate, you can see:
Certificate Name: The name of the root certificate.
Uploaded on: The date and time the root certificate was uploaded.
Expiration Date: The expiration date of the root certificate.
Type: The type of root certificate.
Certificate: The option to download the root certificate.
Download any root certificates that are not the default root certificate.
Edit any root certificates that are not the default root certificate.
Delete any root certificates that are not the default root certificate.
View the full details for the default root certificate.
